summary: Observation of luminous orbs emanating from laser spots
description: On November 24, 1990, in the Nantes region, several witnesses observed about ten luminous spheres moving at high speed. The investigation revealed that these were laser beams installed by EDF (Électricité de France) for the 20th anniversary celebrations of the Cordennais nuclear power plant. These lasers were visible from 40 km away.

summary: Observations of a fireball disintegrating. Probable atmospheric reentry.
description: On November 6, 1990, around 10:00 PM, several witnesses in different departments of southwestern France observed an orange fireball that disintegrated silently. Given the scale of the previous night's atmospheric reentry, this was likely another atmospheric reentry.

summary: Thousands of people witnessed an atmospheric reentry of exceptional magnitude: the 3rd stage of a Soviet PROTON rocket re-entered the atmosphere.
description: It was 8 p.m. on November 5, 1990, when CNES security services were inundated with calls from numerous gendarmerie brigades reporting a strange luminous phenomenon that had crossed a large part of France around 7 p.m. For over a week, SEPRA received numerous calls from witnesses seeking explanations for "a huge luminous triangle" crossing the sky. Among the witnesses, JP Haigneré, an astronaut at CNES, confirmed the strangeness of the phenomenon. At the balloon launch center in Aire-sur-l'Adour, technicians delayed a launch to observe the phenomenon! SEPRA's staff was reinforced for the occasion, and the search for information began with civil and military aviation authorities, meteorological services, and NASA regarding a possible atmospheric reentry. NASA's response arrived on November 8th, indicating that the object "20925/1990 94C / GORIZONT 21 PLATFORM / USSR" had re-entered space on November 5th. The CNES orbitography services confirmed the trajectory of this re-entry, which crossed France from the Bay of Biscay to Alsace. This information was provided to news agencies on November 9th, 1990. It should be noted that a witness, a member of a particularly effective observation network, informed SEPRA as early as November 6th that it was indeed object 90/94C and that it had passed 103 km above the Bay of Biscay before exiting in eastern France at an altitude of 83 km. The flyby of a cloud of debris from a Soviet PROTON third stage rocket occurred at an altitude of 100 to 50 km and at a decreasing speed of 7 to 2 km/s (25,000 to 7,200 km/h). However, a witness, whoever they may be, cannot estimate the distance of an unknown object, let alone points of light, at night. Nevertheless, their brain unconsciously estimates a distance based on the intensity of the light from the phenomenon. (See the explanation on estimating the size and distance of an unknown phenomenon.) This collection of molten debris, followed by trails, stretched across space for several tens of kilometers depending on the shape and composition of the metallic pieces. And it was the intensity of the light from the phenomenon that made it appear close to the witnesses. This proximity illusion is observed with every bolide sighting. This perceptual illusion, known as the distance illusion, is well known to psychologists specializing in visual perception. It is similar to the contour illusion or shape illusion: in this case, when an observer sees a set of points moving together, their brain constructs a virtual object containing those points. See the article on the psychology of form. However, the majority of eyewitness accounts from the atmospheric reentry of November 5, 1990, describe the observation of a dark object, equipped with multiple lights, flying at low altitude from the WSW towards the E-NE. The eyewitness accounts are consistent with the observation of a cloud of molten debris resulting from the fragmentation of the third stage of a PROTON rocket re-entering the atmosphere: - the time and duration of the observation, - the multiple points of light, - the direction of observation: see the new simulation of the atmospheric re-entry of November 5, 1990, - the apparent size (witnesses were surprised to see that the apparent size did not change during the passage: proof that the object was very distant). GEIPAN classifies this case as "A" as an observation of the re-entry into the atmosphere of the third stage of a PROTON rocket. Several witnesses, deeply shocked by their observation, did not accept this explanation.

summary: Observation of a triangular object, the size of an airplane, changing direction and moving silently
description: On October 26, 1990, while returning home from work, a witness driving his car observed a triangular object, the size of an airplane, changing direction and moving silently. The phenomenon could not be identified.

summary: Observation of the rapid passage of a luminous white ball in the sky followed by a luminous trail of the same color: observation of a probable reentry of a meteoroid.
description: On October 20, 1990, between 6:30 and 6:45 PM, a witness and his wife were walking along the Chemin des Romains in Pennautier (11) when a bright white ball of light appeared in the sky. This ball was followed by a luminous trail of the same color. The entire object followed a curved southwest-northeast trajectory and quickly disappeared behind the houses lining the road. No sound was heard. The total duration of the observation is not recorded. Only one witness account was collected. The description of the UFO resembled that of a fireball. Given its moderate strangeness and consistency (single witness), this case appears to be a likely case of mistaken identity with a well-known astronomical phenomenon: the atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid.

summary: Observing a large luminous ball for 5 to 6 minutes
description: On September 26, 1990, at 5:00 PM, a woman was watching television when her attention was drawn to a luminous sphere moving toward her house through her window. Frightened, she called her two neighbors, who witnessed the phenomenon. After ascending, the sphere descended and hovered above a tree. At that moment, it became extremely bright, illuminating the entire area and blinding the witnesses. The entire observation lasted five to six minutes. No explanation could be found for this phenomenon.

summary: Observation of 3 luminous balls in the sky: reflection of light on the clouds.
description: On September 24, 1990, at approximately 10:15 PM, five witnesses were intrigued by three luminous, yellowish-white orbs with blurred outlines, as if seen through the clouds. A sixth witness, living in a nearby town, indicated that these lights were the reflection on the clouds of three large spotlights placed on the ground.

summary: Nighttime observations, in the overcast sky, of the evolutions (back and forth and rotating movements) of an ovoid shape of milky color: probable observations of luminous laser animations (skytracer).
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named THANN (68) 1990, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. On September 19, 1990, at approximately 9:45 PM, a couple and two children observed the movements of a milky white, ovoid shape in the overcast sky. This shape moved and rotated above the MOOSCH forest before disappearing. A neighborhood survey identified four other witnesses who had seen similar phenomena on September 19, 20, and 21. At the time of the observation, GEIPAN had little to no experience with such sightings. The cases accumulated since then (search for cases on www.geipan.fr using the keywords skyrose, skytracer, or laser) confirm that the present observation perfectly matches the hypothesis of a luminous spot on the cloud ceiling created by the use of a ground-based spotlight (see the investigation report): - oval shape, according to the perspective created by the angle of observation; - back-and-forth and rotating movements; - presence of cloud cover; - white color; - brightness and general appearance of the UFO described by the witnesses as opaque, milky, and dull; diffuse light not illuminating the surrounding area. Given this strong correlation, the hypothesis is plausible despite the fact that the observation occurred on a Wednesday evening (and not on a weekend, which would have been more conducive to a festive event) and that no trace of any local or private gathering was found. Indeed, 30 years later, this lack of evidence is not conclusive; nothing allows us to refute the existence of such an event or even a midweek calibration session (which lasted only 15 minutes) for an event held on a weekend, which would not have caused any unusual phenomena in the sky due to different weather conditions. The consistency is sound, with an investigation carried out on site by the Gendarmerie. However, the absence of angular measurements and photographs or videos taken at the time by witnesses is regrettable. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies it as category B: observation of light displays (laser, skytracer).

summary: Observation of an ovoid shape with red and green lights, moving slowly or stationarily.
description: Over several days and for several hours at a time, starting at 9:30 PM, ovoid shapes with red and green lights were observed moving slowly or remaining stationary. This observation was made by several witnesses as well as a patrol of the National Police. The phenomenon could not be identified, although it could be mistaken for lasers from a Lille nightclub. It could also be linked to the observation of July 17th if the hypothesis of aircraft passage is not correct.

summary: Observation of a very bright flash of light with a cadence of approximately 3 seconds
description: On August 23, 1990, at approximately 11:00 PM, a witness observed a very bright flash of light, with a cadence of about 3 seconds, moving very rapidly, lasting 30 to 40 seconds. No further information is available regarding this observation.

summary: Observation of stationary green and red phenomena for a few moments above a farm building
description: On August 19, 1990, around 10:45 PM, a farm owner observed a stationary red shape above a building, followed by a green one. Frightened, he went home. Fireworks had been set off the same day at the same time and may have been the cause of the sighting. The following year, to confirm this hypothesis, the police returned to the farm to observe the effects of the fireworks. The witness did not recognize the sightings from the previous year, but he was not in the same circumstances (he knew what he was going to see), and the fireworks hypothesis remained the most likely.

summary: Observation of a diamond-shaped object flying horizontally with yellow and red lights, moving at very high speed and without noise
description: On the night of July 17-18, 1990, numerous witnesses, including a gendarmerie patrol, observed up to 13 objects moving silently with flashing lights. One witness mentioned a kite-like shape. This was most likely a case of mistaken identity with aircraft. This sighting coincides with the start, on the same day, of the Tour de France air race for young pilots.

summary: Observation of a crater in a field, presumably a bomb from the last war that exploded.
description: On July 11, 1990, SEPRA was informed via the media of the discovery of a large crater in a field. The crater was 14 meters in diameter with a collapsed rim of earth approximately 2.5 meters wide and a central mound 4.5 meters wide and 1.5 meters high. Upon examination of the rocks and large blocks brought up from the subsoil, two hypotheses were considered: the impact of a large meteorite or an underground explosion. A backhoe was brought in to explore the crater, proceeding slowly in layers of 50 to 70 cm. The exploration continued to a depth of 7 meters. As the investigation progressed, fragments of the crater were found at various depths. Twenty-five metallic fragments were recovered, ruling out the meteorite impact hypothesis and suggesting the likely underground explosion of a World War II-era bomb. The fragments were sent to the DGA's (French Directorate General of Armaments) weapons laboratory, whose findings confirmed the hypothesis. Reconstructing the device allowed for the identification of a 250 kg incendiary bomb of British or American origin, probably manufactured in April 1942.

summary: Observation from a sailboat of silent movements in the sky of a luminous oval object with a red light on one side and a green-blue light on the other: very likely sighting of an airplane.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named [MER] LAT 44.76, LON -4.32 (INT) 03.07.1990, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. This case concerns the observation of a UFO by a witness at sea off the Spanish coast on his sailboat, on July 3, 1990, at approximately 10:30 PM. The witness, at the helm, observed for a little over 30 seconds the movements of a luminous oval object with a red light on one side and a blue-green light on the other. No unusual noises were heard, and no disturbances were noticed on the sailboat (engine running and navigation lights on). The witness went to the local Gendarmerie brigade on July 20, 1990. The witness most likely observed an aircraft preparing to land at night with its landing lights on at a Spanish airport (see the investigation report). The presence of red, blue-green, and white (or white-yellow) lights noted by the witness is perfectly characteristic of an aviation-related incident. The red and (blue) green lights are indeed navigation lights. It would appear to be an airplane rather than a helicopter, as the main light, bright like a bulb and forming a horizontal oval, would correspond well to two landing lights of a commercial airliner, close to each other and horizontally aligned, as observed from a distance. The observation distance must be considered in relation to the simultaneous visibility of several types of lights with different power and ranges. The red and green navigation lights, clearly observed here by the witness, have a much more limited range than landing lights, as well as white anti-collision lights, whose characteristic flashing is visible from a great distance, but which were never observed by the witness. International aviation regulations require that navigation lights be switched on at all times, unlike collision avoidance lights, which can be switched off under certain specific conditions such as fog, heavy rain, or when crossing a cloud in IMC flight, where the reflection of light off suspended water droplets could interfere with the pilot's vision. It seems logical to favor the hypothesis that the aircraft was located a few kilometers from the witness rather than a hundred kilometers away, which would have rendered the navigation lights completely invisible. The absence of the collision avoidance lights would therefore be attributable to weather conditions conducive to their temporary extinguishing, conditions that cannot be confirmed or refuted. The landing lights, although they appear to have been switched on (assuming a landing at a Spanish coastal airport) well before landing, can be switched on under other circumstances (congested airspace, low aircraft altitude, or changes in flight level) that could apply to this case. These landing lights have a limited horizontal and vertical field of view, which explains why the witness did not see them illuminate the ocean. The beams of these lights may be invisible because this depends on the presence or absence of airborne particles between the witness and the UAP. The maneuvers of this aircraft, as reconstructed from the witness's statements, are consistent with those that a commercial airliner might perform on approach to an airport (loops, turns), although these maneuvers would have been carried out far from Spanish coastal areas. Thirty years later, it is not possible to obtain traffic records that could either confirm or refute such an aircraft hypothesis. Furthermore, the absence of any perceived noise is not conclusive for the hypothesis, since the noise of the boat's engine (reported by the witness) could have masked any aircraft engine noise, which, moreover, could have been attenuated by a contrary wind. The evidence is weak, with little usable data, but sufficient to validate the hypothesis given its high probability. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: highly probable aircraft sighting.

summary: Recent but imprecise testimony of an old observation of a point of light followed by an account of a strange encounter: lack of information.
description: witness reported in 2012 an observation made between July and August 1990 (the date of July 1, 1990, is given arbitrarily, as the witness did not remember the exact date). This person also linked this first observation to a particular event that occurred in 2005. As a teenager, the witness was stargazing with her brother from their bedroom at around 12:30 a.m. They both noticed a point of light approaching and a gigantic, black, and silent object hovering in front of the house. The children heard voices and, frightened, hid under a desk until the object departed. It was 2:30 a.m. when they emerged from their hiding place, astonished to have remained hidden for so long. One night in 2005, the main witness, waking up very agitated, recalled that during the very long time she and her brother had been hiding, she had boarded the craft. She found herself surrounded by six beings discussing her amongst themselves and that she was completely terrified. The witness suddenly found herself under the desk in the bedroom of the house. The witness recounted a UFO sighting in 1990, then a strange encounter in 2005. The account of both cases was provided for expert analysis to a researcher at the University of Toulouse, a member of a CNRS laboratory, specializing in eyewitness accounts. The result of this analysis concluded that the beginning of the first sighting was genuinely experienced by the witness (the beginning of the testimony suggests a satellite pass). However, the age of the observation and the lack of information (date, time) prevent a clear conclusion. The second experiment is more recent, but the findings highlight strong indicators of non-lived narratives, which are called false memories—that is, memories adopted by the witness in all sincerity, but resulting from an involuntary construction on their part. The appearance of false memories can occur in witnesses who have experienced post-traumatic stress disorder (in this case, the witness retains a traumatic memory of the first experience with repercussions on their health (memory impairment)). This case is classified as "C": unusable due to a lack of precise information.

summary: Observation of three yellow lights rotating constantly along an oval. Disco spotlights.
description: On May 25, 1990, around 11 p.m., several witnesses were intrigued by three yellow spotlights spinning in the sky. The phenomenon was seen by other witnesses over several days. The investigation would unequivocally show that it was a spotlight system from a nearby nightclub, visible from over 30 km away.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric rent
description: On May 26, 1990, at approximately 10:00 PM, a witness and his wife observed a prolonged dark phenomenon involving a rapidly moving orange flame. The witnesses' description strongly suggests that it was an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation of a triangular object with very powerful headlights that remained stationary for a minute, then moved off very quickly
description: On May 4, 1990, at 10:30 PM, a woman observed a silent, triangular object with powerful headlights that hovered for a few moments before moving off very quickly. No further information is available regarding this single witness account.

summary: Observations by 3 witnesses of the silent passage in the sky of a silver-grey hemisphere shape with stems or "tentacles" below: probable observations of a Mylar balloon.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This case, previously classified as D and named MARDIE (45) 02.05.1990, is one of a group of cases recently re-examined. It concerns the observation by three witnesses of a UFO (Unidentified Aerial Phenomenon) from their garden, then from the street in front of their home, in BOU (45), on 02.05.1990 at 9:00 PM. Witnesses describe the silent passage of a silvery-grey oval or hemispherical shape with appendages beneath it, which then disappeared over the horizon. The UFO is described as oval-shaped (although drawings depict it as more of a hemisphere), silvery-grey in color, and having a polished appearance. All three witnesses also note the presence beneath the UFO of what they describe as appendages, rods, or tentacles, as well as light reflection phenomena on its surface, identified by Witness 1 as likely caused by sunlight impacting this surface (see the investigation report). Finally, the UFO is described as being silent and moving at a constant speed. Its movement was in the direction of the light wind. Estimates of the observation duration vary, ranging from one to five minutes. All this data supports the hypothesis of a novelty balloon made of Mylar (reflecting sunlight) moving in a straight line and steadily with the wind. The appendages could therefore be the strings used to hold it on the ground, or a component of the novelty balloon (such as legs for an animal-shaped balloon). Such balloons already existed in 1990. This is an urban area, and it was during the day. Festive or recreational events of this type usually occur on weekends. However, a birthday could also be celebrated on the same day, and there could also have been some kind of event that day in the town or another location further upwind. The fact that nothing can be found nearly 30 years later does not invalidate this hypothesis, which can therefore be considered probable given the strong correlation with the other points. During the initial observation and investigation, GEIPAN had little to no experience with misinterpretations caused by Mylar balloons (see www.geipan.fr for cases recorded since then; search using the keywords "Mylar" or "balloon"). The consistency of the case is moderate, based primarily on the good agreement between the descriptions and sketches of the UFO (Unidentified Aerial Phenomenon) made by witnesses, as well as the maps of the area showing the UFO's trajectory drawn up by the Gendarmerie. GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable Mylar balloon sighting.

summary: Observation of the evolution of a triangular phenomenon with three white points of light and one red point
description: On May 1, 1990, around 11:00 PM, a young couple was driving. The man noticed a stationary red dot in the sky. He stopped to observe it for about ten minutes, during which time the dot remained stationary. Then, the dot moved very quickly laterally before stopping again. After about two minutes, the dot approached the witnesses, who then observed three white lights in the shape of an isosceles triangle, with the red dot in the center. The entire phenomenon flew over the car and sped away. No sound was heard during the entire observation. Despite articles published in the press, no other witnesses could be found, and the phenomenon remains unexplained.

summary: Observation in the Orleans region by 3 independent witnesses of a red light the apparent size of the moon moving diagonally without noise.
description: On April 30, 1990, at approximately 10:30 PM, three independent witnesses observed a red light, roughly the size of the moon, in the Orleans region. The phenomenon moved silently and at an angle toward Earth. One witness reported unusual excitement in their dogs. The event lasted only a few seconds. The witnesses' descriptions suggest an atmospheric reentry, but this could not be definitively identified.

summary: Observation for fifteen minutes of an object emitting flashing lights
description: On April 19, 1990, a witness observed from his home 4 flashing lights for about fifteen minutes.

summary: Observation of a triangular shadow flying at 60 or 80 km/h in the shape of a fish (ray)
description: On April 12, 1990, at 12:17 PM, a witness driving a car was "overflown" by a shadow shaped like a ray (fish) that crossed his path. This rather dark shadow led the witness to believe he had been overflown by a low-flying object traveling at approximately 60 to 80 km/h. No further information could be gathered.

summary: Sighting of a low-flying craft and strange lights
description: On March 22, 1990, three witnesses separately and repeatedly observed a strange luminous phenomenon. One witness reported being flown over by an orange disc that made a strange whirring sound. Frightened, he fell off his moped. Another witness twice saw a similar craft and strange lights behind the hills. The investigation failed to find an explanation for this phenomenon.

summary: Discovery of several circles of dried grass in two fields
description: A farmer noticed a circle of yellowed grass in one of his pastures, approximately 15 to 25 cm wide and nearly 8 meters in diameter. This phenomenon was discovered on two different properties a few weeks apart. An on-site investigation by SEPRA, along with soil analyses conducted by the Rennes School of Agronomy, revealed that it was a fungal infection causing the well-known "fairy ring" phenomenon, in this case, of considerable size. The phenomenon, once clearly identified, was classified as Class A.

summary: Observation of a silent round/oval object with 3 powerful white spotlights
description: On February 27, 1990, a young couple driving by observed an object shaped like a rugby ball with three powerful white spotlights. This object, approximately 2.5 to 3 meters in diameter, flew slowly and silently at a very low altitude. After following the object for about ten minutes, it disappeared at high speed. The investigation failed to identify the object as any known aircraft or any other phenomenon.

summary: Observation of a cylindrical object, 5 to 6 meters in diameter and silent, flying over a school
description: On January 4, 1990, in the courtyard of a middle school around 12:40 PM, about ten children observed a black oval (or cylindrical, according to some accounts) shape, described as having "legs" and "portholes." The object passed silently at an altitude of approximately 150 meters above the school. The alert teachers noticed nothing. On January 16, in a neighboring town, a weather balloon launched from Bordeaux was discovered. Reconstructing the balloon's shape from the debris allowed the observation to be identified as this balloon; the "legs" were in fact the lower part of the radar reflector.

summary: Observation of 3 intense lights in a triangle.
description: witness reports that in 1990 or 1991, while walking down the street, he was dazzled by an object passing in front of the sun. This object was formed by three intense lights that outlined an equilateral triangle. The object moved slowly and made no noise. It had a metallic appearance, was gray in color, and displayed geometric patterns. It suddenly disappeared at an "incredible" speed. This late (April 2008) and poorly documented testimony does not allow us to conduct a serious investigation that could validate or refute certain hypotheses, particularly that of an aircraft passing by.
